reminders.title: Post old LI post on LI around thanksgiving
reminders.info:
To all CRE professionals: On this day 18 years ago…
One year into the business, I still had yet to close a deal. I was always the first one in, the last one out. I worked harder than everyone around me. I stuck to the fundamentals but had yet to find any success. 
Others who had started at the same time or after me were closing deals. Seeing that was starting to take a toll. I was becoming frustrated.
I had one big deal under contract at the time, which would be a turning point to add momentum to my career…Finally allowing me to be debt-free and alleviate some of my financial anxiety.
A little background on the deal. The buyer put down a $500k deposit that was nonrefundable and was closing a couple of weeks after Thanksgiving.
The buyer called me on the Wednesday before Thanksgiving, wanting to cancel the contract… Although he had $500k hard cash in the deal. He wanted his deposit back and threatened to sue everyone involved if he didn’t get it. I was crushed.
Meanwhile, when all of this is happening on the phone, my entire family is inside the house having a great time enjoying Thanksgiving festivities.
I walked back inside and had to explain what had happened, how dejected I was, and how since I had no other listings or escrows. I felt like I was starting over 12 months in. That was my low point.
My blessing was that no one in my family advised me to find another job. No one suggested I stop doing brokerage. Generally, they just shrugged, said, “That sucks,” “Life’s not fair,” and to “stop feeling sorry for myself and deal with it.” So I did. I just kept moving forward.
That was the right move, and that was the right advice to receive at the time. Tough love never feels good. It’s a lot like medicine; tastes bad on the way down but good for you.
Many CRE professionals, brokers, owners, and general real estate entrepreneurs had a tough year this year. This week they are going to sit down with loved ones and have a lot of people very close to them questioning why they are doing what they are doing.
They will hear, “Why don’t you find something else to do? Something with a salary? Something a little safer…?”
That question is going to be thrown at a lot of new agents during this holiday season. Many of you should be prepared to hear it this week, and not only remind them but more importantly remind yourself why you are doing what you are doing.
And my message to all the CRE professionals in their first couple of years in the industry, going through that valley of despair... DO NOT QUIT, DO NOT STOP, KEEP MOVING FORWARD…IT WILL PAY OFF! I don’t know if it will be in 2 years, 3 years, or 5 years…but it will pay off. There is a pot of gold at the end of this rainbow.
Also, FWIW I ended up selling that deal three years later and making an even larger commission down the road. Stick to the fundamentals, keep fighting, and I’m telling you from my personal experience you will make it through.
KM
